newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Life profits lift GA to record.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Life profits lift GA to record.

text.p: Britain's General Accident Plc on Tuesday ruled out an acquisition to bolster its fast growing life operations, at least in the short term.
But the Perth, Scotland-based insurer said it expected life profits to continue to enjoy the healthy growth seen in the first half over the remainder of 1997.
The comments came as GA reported record operating profits for the first half of 260 million pounds ($411 million), up from 193 million pounds last year.
The figures were toward the top end of analyst forecasts and GA shares added 14 pence to 959 pence.

Life profits rose 37 percent to 63 million pounds, reflecting the absence of integration costs associated with last year's Provident Mutual acquisition and the benefits of focusing on growing the business.
Sales of life and pensions products rose 19 percent with a similar increase in the profitability of new business.
Chief executive Bob Scott said the group would concentrate on getting the full benefits from Provident before looking at other acquisitions.
GA has set itself the target of doubling business from sales of life assurance, pension and investment products over the next three years.

In May, it said it hoped to buy two companies, one dealing in life and the other a general insurance concern with small business expertise. But it stressed then that it would not be rushed into purchases.
The general insurance market remained in the doldrums over the first half with all GA's major territories highly competitive.
Net written premiums fell to 2,210 million pounds from 2,230 million pounds while the worldwide underwriting deficit reduced to 66 million pounds from 105 million pounds.
The underwriting improvement included a 40 million pound decline in severe weather-related losses to 50 million pounds.
While the UK increased underwriting profits to 19 million pounds, Scott said that rate increases were proving increasingly hard.
Overseas markets were similarly competitive with the U.S. unable to break out of its long down cycle and Canada difficult.
There were signs of rate increases being applied by a number of companies in UK private motor, but not in other product lines.
Increases in personal and commercial premiums by GA had stuck but it had lost some business in commercial as a result of the rise, said Scott.
Like rivals, GA had seen a sharp increase in UK property subsidence costs to 12 million pounds, a rise of 50 percent from last year.
A similar increase is expected over the full year.
In the U.S. it was proving very hard to get rate increases, said Scott.
GA was attacking the poorly performing homeowners account and was also putting rate increase on commercial property, he said.
However, the U.S. produced an improved underwriting result, reflecting reduced severe weather costs.
Investment earnings in the half year grew seven percent in original currencies, partly reflecting the move from equities into higher yielding bonds.
Total pre-tax profits, including realised investment gains of 334 million pounds rose to 580 million pounds from 335 million pounds.
The increase in realised investment gains reflects GA's decision to reduce its exposure to equity markets.
Net asset value per share rose to 784 pence by August 8 from 675 pence at the end of 1996.
The interim dividend was raised 10 percent to 12.5 pence per share. ($ = 0.632 British Pounds)
